task: Task 6 — Refactor job() into prep-only + cron bump + delete process_new_articles
summary: The prep-phase refactor doesn't introduce any new authentication, authorisation, or network surface — it moves code that was already trusted into a staging shape. Every exception surface that could carry a secret is fed through sanitize_error_message (Decision 11). SQL writes go through the pending_articles_repo parameterised-query layer from Task 1 — no new inline SQL in job(). No unvalidated user input reaches the DB; the fetcher-supplied entries are trusted the same way they were under the old process_new_articles path.

owasp_mapped_checks.A03_injection: Pass. All DB writes go through pending_articles_repo.insert_pending / list_pending / get_pending / list_pending_stale / list_notified_overdue — all `?`-parameterised (audited in Task 1). The only new SQL in news_bot is the existing processed_news DDL (constant) + delegated init_schema. No f-string interpolation into SQL.
owasp_mapped_checks.A04_insecure_design: Pass. Cron bump to hourly is a deliberate follow-up on the 2h grace window (Decision 5); failure-in-source isolation + admin-ping on failure matches existing pattern.
owasp_mapped_checks.A05_security_misconfiguration: Pass. IDLE_TIMEOUT_HOURS / GRACE_WINDOW_HOURS / QUEUE_CAP env-parsed with explicit `int()` coercion (defined in Task 3) — no boolean-mode drift.
owasp_mapped_checks.A08_software_and_data_integrity_failures: Pass. insert_pending UNIQUE-conflict path is defensive; upstream source modules (mattel_news_source et al) own HTML-parsing hardening and weren't touched.
owasp_mapped_checks.A09_security_logging_monitoring: Pass. Every error path logs through the module logger at ERROR (fetcher failures, insert failures, notify failures, list_pending failures). sanitize_error_message scrubs the four env-secrets before any string reaches the log or admin chat.

secret_handling.db_writes: insert_pending receives only fetcher-sourced fields (title/paragraphs/images/blocks/subtitle/pub_date) plus the derived source_name. No error strings or tokens hit `pending_articles` via this path.
secret_handling.admin_chat_writes: Two call sites: (a) per-source failure ping — passes `sanitize_error_message(exc)`; (b) queue-status ping via `build_admin_ping(rows)` — builds from sanitised source_name / title only, no error text. Both wrapped in try/except so a Telegram failure can't propagate a token.
secret_handling.logger_writes: All ERROR paths on exceptions use `sanitize_error_message` before f-string interpolation.

findings.description: The `f"⚠️ Source {fetcher_name} failed: {safe}"` admin ping is Markdown-parsed by `send_admin_notification` (`parse_mode='Markdown'`). A malicious exception message that includes Markdown control chars (backticks, asterisks, square brackets) could lightly disrupt formatting — but cannot execute code and cannot leak secrets (`sanitize_error_message` is already applied).
findings.recommendation: No action. Telegram Markdown is non-executable and the pre-existing load_feeds admin-ping is the same shape. Hardening Markdown escaping is orthogonal and larger than this task.

findings.description: `fetch_full_article` returns user-controllable strings (title/paragraphs/images/blocks) that land in `pending_articles` TEXT columns. Because everything is SQLite-parameterised, there's no SQLi vector. Downstream Task 2's `preview_renderer` enforces tag+URL-scheme allowlists; downstream Task 8's publisher passes through telegraph_publisher's existing allowlists. No new surface in Task 6.
findings.recommendation: No action. The validation is at the rendering/publishing layer, which is unchanged.

findings.description: init_db opens a connection and delegates to pending_articles_repo.init_schema, which also commits and the outer init_db commits again. SQLite transactions aren't nested — the second commit is a no-op. No security impact; logged here for completeness in case a future reviewer sees two commits and wonders.

pending-filter issues one `get_pending(link)` per candidate — N+1 query pattern. For QUEUE_CAP=10 this is at most ~15 queries per tick, well within budget. If QUEUE_CAP is raised to 1000 via env override the cost stays linear in the number of fresh candidates per tick, still negligible for the hourly cadence.
findings.recommendation: No action. Performance characterisation is acceptable for expected scales; Task 10's overflow path will itself loop the queue and is the right place to consider batch pre-fetch.
